subject: Next steps & mutual action plan — procurement path (PO vs card) and marketplace interest
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + MPA / procurement path questions

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap from our side and suggested mutual action plan (MAP) so we keep momentum on the procurement front. We heard that Acme is evaluating Redwood for a fraud-detection pilot and you wanted clarity on the commercial path (PO vs card) and whether AWS Marketplace is interesting from your sourcing perspective.

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft), Redwood_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (security evidence), MPA_Draft_v2.docx (brief MAP).

Proposed MAP (high level) — target pilot start: mid-Jan 2027
- Week 0: SOW alignment + signatures (you / us) — owner: Monica / Sara
- Week 1–2: Legal review (redlines) — owner: Acme Legal / Redwood contracts
- Week 2–3: Security review (SOC2 evidence, network questions) — owner: Acme Security (Lina) / Redwood security
- Week 3–4: Finance & procurement approval (PO issuance or card setup) — owner: Acme Finance / Neha (finance lead)
- Week 4+: Provisioning & pilot kick-off (access, keys, onboarding) — owner: Redwood solutions (Priyom)

Questions for you so we can finalize timing:
1) Preferred commercial instrument for the pilot: PO (standard procurement) or corporate card for faster start?
2) Is AWS Marketplace required/desired for procurement, or would a direct PO to Redwood be fine?
3) Who are the primary reviewers we should expect for Legal and Security (names + timelines)?

If PO is preferred, what is Acme's usual legal review SLA? If you prefer card for the pilot, we can offer a 90-day pilot invoice and onboarding checklist to speed things up.

Next step: Can you confirm the preferred procurement path by EOD Wednesday (12/01)? Once we have that, Ben and I will queue the SOW and contract route and Priyom will prep access steps.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0123
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmefin.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Park <john.park@acmefin.com> (Legal), Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acmefin.com> (Security)
Date: 2026-11-29T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + MPA / procurement path questions

Monica —

Appreciate the clear MAP. A few answers from our side:
- Procurement instrument: acme prefers a PO for anything that will be onboarded into our environment long-term; however, for an initial 6–8 week pilot we're open to paying by corporate card to accelerate start (finance will need to approve the spend).
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred for our Procurement Ops team because it simplifies invoicing and procurement reconciliation. If Redwood can publish a listing or provide a Marketplace-ready configuration, that would be our preference.
- Reviewers / SLAs: Legal (John Park) typically has a 7–10 business day SLA for first-pass redlines on straightforward SOWs, Security (Lina) expects 5–7 business days to review SOC2 artifacts and our network checklist, Finance can turn a PO in 3–5 business days once Legal signs off. All timelines assume no substantive redlines.

I'll introduce Finance and Procurement contacts if we move to a PO. For the pilot, card payment would be fastest; if Redwood can accept a card invoice and provide an onboarding checklist we can target a Dec 20th start for an expedited pilot.

I'll check with Lina about any additional security artifacts she needs and get back to you.

Best,
Sara
Director, Procurement Programs | Acme Financial Services
sara.nguyen@acmefin.com | +1 212 555 3398

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T12:42:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Acme - procurement path and next internal asks

Team — quick internal summary following Sara's note:
- Acme prefers PO for long-term but will accept card for pilot to accelerate. They want AWS Marketplace if available.
- Timeline expectations they gave:
  * Legal: 7–10 biz days
  * Security: 5–7 biz days
  * Finance/PO issuance: 3–5 biz days post-legal

Action items (owners):
- Contracts (Ben): prepare an SOW + slim MSA addendum optimized for a pilot (target 1 page of redlines). Push for quick review.
- Solutions (Priyom): prepare onboarding checklist + provisioning runbook and a Marketplace packaging checklist (what we need to list on AWS).
- Security (Monica/Priyom): provide SOC2 pointer docs and network diagram; Priyom to ask infra for ephemeral creds flow for pilot.
- Finance (Neha): confirm our ability to accept card for pilot and terms for a 90-day pilot invoice. Also confirm if we can create an AWS Marketplace listing timeline (marketplace billing flow).

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0832

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmefin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + MPA / procurement path questions — Draft MAP attached

Hi Sara —

Looping back with a slightly updated Mutual Action Plan (attached) that maps owners and expected dates based on the SLAs you shared. I've included two procurement tracks so you can pick the path you prefer:

Track A — PO path (standard)
- Day 0: Confirm SOW + signatures
- Day 1–10: Legal review (Acme) — owner: John Park
- Day 3–12: Security review — owner: Lina Gomez (Acme) / Redwood security
- Day 13–16: Finance approvals and PO issuance — owner: Acme Finance
- Day 17: Provisioning kickoff

Track B — Card-first pilot (fast-start)
- Day 0: Confirm SOW and card billing details
- Day 1–3: Redwood issues invoice; Finance approves card charge
- Day 4: Provisioning & pilot start

We also included an AWS Marketplace column — minimal changes required on our side but we'd need your procurement ops to provide the Marketplace billing entity and any catalog metadata.

Could you confirm which track you prefer and share the names for Procurement Ops so we can start the Marketplace thread if that's the route? Happy to jump on a quick 30-minute call to finalize.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0199
